description: Calculating totals discounts and interest using the four basic operations
problem_example: A store applies a 15% discount to a $80 item. What is the final price?

description: Using linear equations to relate distance speed and time
problem_example: A car travels at 60 km/h for t hours. Express the distance d as a function of t.

description: Finding straight-line distance between two GPS coordinates
problem_example: Two cities are at (3,4) and (7,1) on a scaled map. Find their straight-line distance.

description: Checking that a right angle is true in building and surveying
problem_example: A builder needs a right angle. She measures 3m and 4m sides. The diagonal must be exactly 5m.

description: Measuring the height of an inaccessible object using similar triangle ratios
problem_example: A 2m pole casts a 3m shadow. A tree casts an 18m shadow. How tall is the tree?

description: Calculating roof pitch and rafter length from angle measurements
problem_example: A roof rises at 30°. If the horizontal span is 8m what is the rafter length?

description: Modelling alternating current as a sinusoidal function using the unit circle
problem_example: Voltage in an AC circuit: V(t) = 220·sin(2π·50·t). Find V at t = 0.005s.

description: Expressing supply and demand as functions of price
problem_example: If demand D(p) = 500 - 3p find the quantity demanded at p = 40.

description: Velocity as the limit of the average velocity as time interval approaches zero
problem_example: A particle's position is s(t) = t². Find its instantaneous velocity at t = 3 as a limit.

description: Checking that a control system's output function has no discontinuous jumps
problem_example: A voltage regulator must output a continuous signal. Why does continuity matter for its design?

description: Velocity is the first derivative and acceleration the second derivative of position
problem_example: A ball has position s(t) = 5t² - 20t + 4. Find its velocity and acceleration at t = 2s.

description: Finding marginal revenue by differentiating a polynomial revenue function
problem_example: If revenue R(q) = 80q - q² find the marginal revenue function and maximising quantity.

description: Differentiating a product of two time-varying quantities
problem_example: Angular momentum L = I·ω. Find dL/dt when I and ω are both functions of t.

description: Differentiating a ratio of concentrations or rates
problem_example: If a reaction rate R = [A]/[B] and both concentrations change find dR/dt.

description: Differentiating position when it depends on an intermediate variable
problem_example: Pressure p depends on altitude h which depends on time t. Find dp/dt.

description: Finding how cost changes with time through an intermediate production variable
problem_example: Revenue R depends on price p which depends on advertising spend s. Find dR/ds.

description: Modelling periodic phenomena such as sound waves and oscillations
problem_example: The displacement of a pendulum: x(t) = A·cos(ωt + φ). Model its motion.

description: Finding velocity of a simple harmonic oscillator by differentiating displacement
problem_example: If x(t) = 3·sin(2t) find the velocity dx/dt and maximum speed.

description: Modelling exponential bacterial or population growth
problem_example: A bacteria culture starts at 100 and doubles every 2 hours. Write P(t) and find P at t=6h.

description: The decibel scale uses logarithms to compress a wide range of sound intensities
problem_example: A sound at 10⁻⁵ W/m² has what dB level? Use L = 10·log₁₀(I/I₀) where I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m².

description: Finding slope of a tangent to a circle without explicitly solving for y
problem_example: Find the slope of the tangent to x² + y² = 25 at the point (3,4).

description: Differentiating production isoquants to find marginal rate of substitution
problem_example: For Q = K^0.5·L^0.5 = 100 find dK/dL to measure how capital substitutes for labour.

description: How fast does the top of a sliding ladder descend as the base moves outward?
problem_example: A 10m ladder leans against a wall. Its base slides outward at 1 m/s. How fast is the top descending when the base is 6m from the wall?

description: Rate at which the radius of an inflating balloon grows from a known volume rate
problem_example: Air is pumped into a sphere at 5 cm³/s. How fast is the radius increasing when r = 3cm?

description: How fast does water level drop in a draining conical tank?
problem_example: A conical tank (h=4m r=2m) drains at 2 m³/min. How fast is the water level falling when h=3m?

description: Finding the output level that maximises profit by setting the derivative to zero
problem_example: If profit P(q) = -q³ + 9q² - 15q - 8 find the production level that maximises profit.

description: Classifying whether a critical point is a maximum (strongest) or minimum (weakest)
problem_example: A beam's deflection function has a critical point. Use the second derivative to determine if it is a maximum deflection.

description: Designing the most material-efficient cylindrical can for a fixed volume
problem_example: A can must hold exactly 355 mL. Find the radius and height that minimise the total surface area.

description: Maximising fenced area using a fixed length of fencing along a barn wall
problem_example: A farmer has 200m of fencing for a rectangular paddock against a barn. What dimensions maximise the area?

description: Maximising box volume by choosing the optimal corner cut from a sheet
problem_example: From a 40cm×30cm sheet squares of side x are cut from corners and folded up. Find x that maximises volume.

description: Identifying increasing and decreasing returns by sketching the marginal cost curve
problem_example: Sketch C(q) = q³ - 6q² + 9q + 5 identifying all critical points and inflection points.

description: Work done by a variable force equals the integral of force over displacement
problem_example: A spring (k=500 N/m) is compressed 0.2m from rest. Calculate the work done using integration.

description: Finding the position function by integrating the velocity function
problem_example: If v(t) = 6t² - 4t find the position function s(t) given that s(0) = 2.

description: Consumer surplus is the definite integral between the demand curve and market price
problem_example: Given D(p) = 100 - 2p and market price p = 20 compute the consumer surplus using a definite integral.

description: Computing power integrals in AC circuits requires u-substitution
problem_example: Evaluate ∫sin²(ωt)dt which arises when computing average AC power.

description: Evaluating integrals of exponential times polynomial functions in circuit analysis
problem_example: Evaluate ∫t·e^(-2t)dt which appears in the step response of an RL circuit.

description: Using the FTC to find net displacement from a velocity function over a time interval
problem_example: A particle has v(t) = 3t² - 2t. Find the net displacement from t=0 to t=3 using the FTC.

description: Deadweight loss is the area between supply and demand curves after a price floor or ceiling
problem_example: Find the area between D(p)=100-2p and S(p)=20+p to measure market surplus.

description: Computing the volume of a conical or paraboloid-shaped container by revolution
problem_example: Find the volume of the solid formed by rotating y=√x around the x-axis from x=0 to x=4.

description: Series are used to analyse the running time of recursive algorithms
problem_example: The number of operations in a recursive algorithm: T(n) = 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + … Evaluate this geometric series.

description: Determining whether perturbation series in quantum mechanics converge
problem_example: Does the series Σ(1/n²) converge? Apply the p-test: p=2 > 1 so it converges.

description: Calculators and software use Taylor series to evaluate sin cos ln and exp
problem_example: How does a CPU compute sin(0.1) without geometric construction? Via Taylor: sin(x) ≈ x - x³/6 + x⁵/120.

description: Marginal utility with respect to each good is a partial derivative of the utility function
problem_example: If U(x,y) = x^0.5·y^0.5 find ∂U/∂x and ∂U/∂y — the marginal utilities of each good.

description: The centre of mass of a 2D lamina is computed using double integrals
problem_example: Find the centre of mass of a uniform lamina over the region 0≤x≤2 0≤y≤3.

description: Divergence and curl describe sources and rotation in fluid velocity fields
problem_example: Given velocity field F = (x²,y²,z²) compute ∇·F and ∇×F to analyse the fluid flow.
